title: Usage-indexed private licensing with upgrade rings and support tier experiment
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Goal: Validate a usage-indexed license fee model for Private/VPC/on-prem customers combined with a three-tier support offering and a staggered upgrade ring cadence. We want to reduce friction for mid-market customers who need predictable unit economics while preserving enterprise SLAs for large customers.

Hypothesis: A base license fee + usage index (GPU-hours or token-equivalents) will increase deal velocity with mid-market buyers by 20% compared to flat seatless commits, while tiered support add-ons will maintain gross margin. Staggered upgrade rings (Fast/Standard/Conservative) will decrease upgrade rollback incidents by 30% and reduce ops load during major runtime releases.

Proposed structure (experimentable knobs):
- License: base annual platform fee (banded by peak reserved capacity) + usage index measured monthly (GPU-hour buckets with overage pricing). Optional pre-purchased credit packs for burst.
- Support tiers: "Core" (business hours triage, 24h response P2), "Priority" (24/7 P1, monthly health reviews), "Critical" (named SRE, guaranteed incident swimlanes, 15-min P1).
- Upgrade rings: Fast (auto-upgrade within 2 weeks), Standard (auto-upgrade within 6 weeks), Conservative (manual opt-in; receives security patches only).

Success metrics:
- Primary: conversion rate from PoC to paid for private offers (+15-25% target), average ARR per deal, NPS for private customers.
- Secondary: reduction in major upgrade rollbacks, reduction in operator tickets per upgrade window, license gross margin.

Telemetry & experiments:
- Track signed deals and map to selected support tier and upgrade ring.
- Dashboard to show usage index distribution (primary metric: 95th percentile monthly GPU-hours).
- A/B test two offer pages: (A) base fee + usage index; (B) flat higher base fee with no usage index.

Implementation plan (next 6 sprints):
1) Legal & Pricing (week 1-3): draft contract appendix and sample SOW language for usage index and upgrade consent. Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PRIVATE/PM-903211+Pricing+Appendix
2) Billing Integration (week 2-5): biller mapping for usage index units and overage thresholds; small schema changes to billing events. GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/issues/482
3) Console UI (week 3-8): support-tier selector, upgrade ring controls, and billing preview on the Private onboarding flow. Design spec: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdEF_pm903211
4) Sales enablement & contracts (week 4-9): create pricing cheat sheet, TCV calculator, and sample contract clauses for enterprise legal.
5) Pilot & telemetry (week 8-12): run pilot with 4 customers (2 mid-market, 2 enterprise) and collect usage curves; run PoC A/B offer for qualifying leads.

Stakeholders: Sales (Evelyn Park), Legal (Samir Bhatia), Engineering Billing (ENG-1842 owner: Jonas Meyer), Console UX (DES-7812 owner: Priyanka Rao), Customer Success (Liam O'Neal).

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: Customers misunderstand usage index leading to billing disputes. Mitigation: billing preview + monthly usage report + two-week overage grace period.
- Risk: Enterprise legal pushback on auto-upgrades. Mitigation: manual opt-out and contractual upgrade windows for Conservative ring.
- Risk: Support capacity mis-sizing. Mitigation: pilot limited to 4 customers and reserved SRE time for Critical tier signups.

Notes: This experiment intersects with security questionnaire updates; Legal requested a short appendix to the procurement QA that clarifies upgrade ring behavior and data residency guarantees. See Security QA draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/SQ+Appendix+PM-903211
